title: Dasakam 28 — Lakṣmīsvayaṃvaram and Amṛtotpatti
description: Shiva accepts the ocean poison; celestial treasures and Lakshmi emerge, Lakshmi chooses Vishnu, and Dhanvantari rises carrying nectar.

source.commentary: intake/D028/photo-captions.txt; caption export and post provenance retained under content/sources/d028

translation_note: No sourced English verse translation is supplied. Commentary is preserved supplied photo-caption text, not a verse translation. Published Sanskrit/IAST line breaks, doubled hyphen continuations and ṁ spellings are retained without silent normalization.

stanzas.sanskrit:
गरलं तरलानलं पुरस्ता-
-ज्जलधेरुद्विजगाल कालकूटम् ।
अमरस्तुतिवादमोदनिघ्नो
गिरिशस्तन्निपपौ भवत्प्रियार्थम् ॥ २८-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
garalaṁ taralānalaṁ purastā-
-jjaladherudvijagāla kālakūṭam |
amarastutivādamodanighno
giriśastannipapau bhavatpriyārtham || 28-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Devas and Asuras churned the milk ocean with the help of the Lord. First, Kalakoota poison emerged which was swallowed by Lord Shiva with great mercy for the mankind.

stanzas.sanskrit:
विमथत्सु सुरासुरेषु जाता
सुरभिस्तामृषिषु न्यधास्त्रिधामन् ।
हयरत्नमभूदथेभरत्नं
द्युतरुश्चाप्सरसः सुरेषु तानि ॥ २८-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vimathatsu surāsureṣu jātā
surabhistāmṛṣiṣu nyadhāstridhāman |
hayaratnamabhūdathebharatnaṁ
dyutaruścāpsarasaḥ sureṣu tāni || 28-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Next came, 
the divine cow - Kamadhenu
 the beautiful horse - Uchchaishravas 
the great elephant - Iravatham
Kalpaka vrusha 
Apsaras came too. 
All of them were gifted to Gods & sages.

stanzas.sanskrit:
जगदीश भवत्परा तदानीं
कमनीया कमला बभूव देवी ।
अमलामवलोक्य यां विलोलः
सकलोऽपि स्पृहयाम्बभूव लोकः ॥ २८-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
jagadīśa bhavatparā tadānīṁ
kamanīyā kamalā babhūva devī |
amalāmavalokya yāṁ vilolaḥ
sakalo’pi spṛhayāmbabhūva lokaḥ || 28-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: As the ocean was churned further, Goddess Mahalakshmi appeared. Her magical form attracted everyone.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वयि दत्तहृदे तदैव देव्यै
त्रिदशेन्द्रो मणिपीठिकां व्यतारीत् ।
सकलोपहृताभिषेचनीयै-
-रृषयस्तां श्रुतिगीर्भिरभ्यषिञ्चन् ॥ २८-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvayi dattahṛde tadaiva devyai
tridaśendro maṇipīṭhikāṁ vyatārīt |
sakalopahṛtābhiṣecanīyai-
-rṛṣayastāṁ śrutigīrbhirabhyaṣiñcan || 28-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: The Goddess who had set her heart on Bhagwan was given a bejewelled throne by Indra. With the objects which everyone had brought, the sages consecrated her and   sang Vedas.
The divine sages did abhishekam to Goddess Lakshmi with holy Ganga water. Goddess Mahalakshmi decked with studded earrings, yellow garment and necklaces appeared enchanting.

stanzas.sanskrit:
वरणस्रजमात्तभृङ्गनादां
दधती सा कुचकुम्भमन्दयाना ।
पदशिञ्जितमञ्जुनूपुरा त्वां
कलितव्रीलविलासमाससाद ॥ २८-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
varaṇasrajamāttabhṛṅganādāṁ
dadhatī sā kucakumbhamandayānā |
padaśiñjitamañjunūpurā tvāṁ
kalitavrīlavilāsamāsasāda || 28-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Goddess Mahalakshmi with extreme devotion approached to Bhagwan  with the divine garland in her hand.

stanzas.sanskrit:
गिरिशद्रुहिणादिसर्वदेवान्
गुणभाजोऽप्यविमुक्तदोषलेशान् ।
अवमृश्य सदैव सर्वरम्ये
निहिता त्वय्यनयाऽपि दिव्यमाला ॥ २८-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
giriśadruhiṇādisarvadevān
guṇabhājo’pyavimuktadoṣaleśān |
avamṛśya sadaiva sarvaramye
nihitā tvayyanayā’pi divyamālā || 28-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Goddess Lakshmi realised that all other Gods as Shiva Brahmaa and others though endowed with virtues, were not free from all defects. Bhagwan Vishnu who was perfect in every way, she put the divine garland on Bhagwan.

stanzas.sanskrit:
उरसा तरसा ममानिथैनां
भुवनानां जननीमनन्यभावाम् ।
त्वदुरोविलसत्तदीक्षणश्री
परिवृष्ट्या परिपुष्टमास विश्वम् ॥ २८-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
urasā tarasā mamānithaināṁ
bhuvanānāṁ jananīmananyabhāvām |
tvadurovilasattadīkṣaṇaśrī
parivṛṣṭyā paripuṣṭamāsa viśvam || 28-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan  readily accepted Goddess Mahalakshmi on Bhagwan’s bosom giving her due respect and honor as she was solely devoted. Her compassionate glances brought prosperity to the whole world.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अतिमोहनविभ्रमा तदानीं
मदयन्ती खलु वारुणी निरागात् ।
तमसः पदवीमदास्त्वमेना
मतिसम्माननया महासुरेभ्यः ॥ २८-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
atimohanavibhramā tadānīṁ
madayantī khalu vāruṇī nirāgāt |
tamasaḥ padavīmadāstvamenā
matisammānanayā mahāsurebhyaḥ || 28-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Next the Goddess Varuni, the deity for wine came, who was intoxicating in appearence and is a source of all  sins. Bhagwan presented her to the asuras as they are the seat of ignorance.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तरुणाम्बुदसुन्दरस्तदा त्वं
ननु धन्वन्तरिरुत्थितोऽम्बुराशेः ।
अमृतं कलशे वहन् कराभ्या-
-मखिलार्तिं हर मारुतालयेश ॥ २८-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
taruṇāmbudasundarastadā tvaṁ
nanu dhanvantarirutthito’mburāśeḥ |
amṛtaṁ kalaśe vahan karābhyā-
-makhilārtiṁ hara mārutālayeśa || 28-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Dhanvanthri, a beautiful form of Lord, finally appeared from the ocean carrying the divine nectar in his hands. Bhattathiri praises Bhagwan for having made world get such priceless gifts by his mercy and requests that he cure him of his ailments.
